basis: Hair/nail dysplasia and chronic neutropenia with recurrent infections define the syndrome; developmental and conjunctival findings lack reliable prevalence or diagnostic-criterion evidence.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental delay and mild ID are reported, but frequency is unspecified and neither >=30% prevalence nor major diagnostic-criterion status is established.

basis: Adrenal medullary tumour; secondary hypertension (~80-90%) is separately diagnosed. Direct cardiomyopathy occurs in a minority (<15%). Neural crest origin does not imply neurologic injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: secondary hypertension (~80-90%) is a separate diagnosis; direct cardiac injury such as catecholamine cardiomyopathy is uncommon (<15%).

basis: DiGeorge-2 deletion phenotype includes developmental impairment, parathyroid and thymic deficiency; congenital heart defects are a major diagnostic feature, supporting cardiovascular involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac malformations are a major feature of the DiGeorge-2 phenotype associated with this deletion; diagnostic significance supports inclusion despite variable frequency.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hypoparathyroidism from parathyroid hypoplasia is a defining component of the DiGeorge-2 deletion phenotype.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: thymic hypoplasia with T-cell immunodeficiency is a defining DiGeorge-2 component; the immunodeficiency mechanism axis applies.

basis: Permanent neonatal diabetes and accompanying liver dysfunction define this syndrome. Explicit hepatic loss of function supports primary hepatic despite its transient course.

decisions.hepatic: primary: liver dysfunction is explicitly named and described in the definition; it represents organ dysfunction, rather than a nonspecific transient sign.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, leukodystrophy and optic atrophy are defining features. Hypopigmentation occurs only in some patients and does not establish common skin damage.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is expressly included among the disorder's defining features and constitutes direct optic nerve damage on the ocular axis.

basis: Chronic venous valve damage defines the syndrome; persistent stasis dermatitis and skin induration are major diagnostic features. Ulceration alone affects a minority (<10%).

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent stasis dermatitis and induration are major diagnostic skin manifestations of chronic venous injury; this does not rely on ulcer frequency (<10%).

basis: Developmental delay 7/7; structural heart defects are a Noonan diagnostic feature (ASD/MVP each 2/7, ~29%); ptosis 6/7 and pes planus 3/7 support ocular and skeletal involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital structural heart defects are a major Noonan diagnostic feature; ASD and mitral prolapse each occur in 2/7 (~29%), approximately the threshold, with overlap unknown.

basis: Congenitally shortened/malrotated intestine causes intestinal failure. Acidosis (3/3) accompanies diarrhoea/dehydration; persistent additional metabolic dysfunction is not established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: acidosis in 3/3 establishes frequency, but intestinal losses and dehydration can cause transient acidosis; persistent metabolic injury or a defining metabolic disorder is not established.

basis: Histoplasma infection usually establishes its primary focus in the lungs. Pulmonary is an origin/site label; disseminated CNS, ocular and other organ disease affects a minority across the umbrella.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: the lungs are the usual primary site of Histoplasma infection, including subclinical pulmonary infection; the >=30% damage test applies to additional involved organs.

basis: Epithelioid sarcoma commonly originates in extremity dermis/subcutis and fascia or tendon-associated connective tissue; these are primary tumour sites rather than metastatic complications.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: dermis and subcutis are characteristic sites of origin for the usual distal form, which predominates across the umbrella; proximal deep-tissue cases do not negate this.
